judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant of coverage turns on undefined boundary phrases — 'excess liability policies written on an occurrence or a claims made basis' and underlying insurance which 'afford limits not less than' the Schedule — so the reach of the cession can be argued either way. The date trigger ('policies becoming effective on or after the effective date and prior to the termination date') is workable but carries the usual attachment-date fight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 4 (c070) substitutes this whole paragraph for policies effective on or after October 1, 1996, and the Stipulation of Termination (c099) speaks of policies 'issued' rather than 'becoming effective', leaving the temporal scope to be reconciled across three instruments. Article XI (c033) also extends the agreement to in-force policies past the termination date, which sits awkwardly with the 'prior to the termination date' cut-off here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Schedule mixes measurement units — 'each occurrence' for GL and auto but 'each medical incident' for Hospital Professional Liability — without defining either, and the aircraft/heliport figures ($10M/$5M underlying) are unusually large for an underlying schedule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article III (c012/c056/c076) states the reinsurance limits in 'each occurrence' terms only, and Amendment No. 4 (c076) deems each claim an occurrence, so the 'medical incident' unit here has no counterpart in the limits article. Amendment No. 4(B) (c071) adds two overlapping entries to this Schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Treating a discovery period or extended reporting endorsement as 'part of the period of said policy' while allowing that 'a separate Limit of liability may apply in respect thereof' is permissive and self-qualifying — whether a fresh limit attaches is left genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Article XI (c033), which continues coverage for discovery periods attaching to policies in force at cancellation, and with the Claim-Conversion Factors in Rating Schedule-B (c086), which promise a free extended reporting endorsement; whether a second full limit is thereby ceded without premium is not resolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence incorporation of two named attachments; nothing in it to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Nuclear Incident Exclusion Clauses and the Insolvency Clause do in fact appear in the document, and the Insolvency Clause is cross-referenced in Article IV (c013), so the incorporation is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Teaching hospital', 'children's hospital' and 'psychiatric hospital' are undefined classifications, and 'operation by the insured of' leaves unclear whether partial teaching activity at a general hospital triggers the exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c053) deletes this exclusion for policies effective on or after July 1, 1995 and narrows it to 'operation of a teaching hospital', so which text governs a given ceded policy depends on layering the amendments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision supplies its own definition of 'total beds' by enumeration, which materially reduces the ambiguity, though the definition mixes 'occupied' acute care beds with unqualified counts of the other categories.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c054) replaces the 250-bed threshold with 350 beds for later policies, so the two thresholds coexist in the instrument and must be sorted by attachment date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Ownership, operation or use of helicopters owned or leased by the insured hospital' is reasonably concrete, with the qualifier limiting it to the hospital's own aircraft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article I (c001) expressly extends the agreement to Heliport Liability and the Schedule of Underlying Limits (c002) sets a $5,000,000 heliport limit, so the interplay between covered heliport exposure and excluded helicopter operations is a genuine point of friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed geographic list of named counties; little to construe on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c055) replaces this list, dropping Cuyahoga County and adding Michigan counties, while Rating Schedule-A (c061) prices Cleveland as Territory 3 — so the original list is superseded but remains in the instrument for earlier policies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The catch-all 'or other combination of insurers or reinsurers formed for the purpose of covering specific coverages, specific lines of business or ... specified geographical areas' sits after an enumerated list (pool, syndicate, association, insolvency fund, guaranty fund), a classic ejusdem generis scope question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nuclear Incident Exclusion Clause No. 2(1) (c043) covers similar pool/association liability, and exclusion (f) (c010) covers assumed reinsurance, so there is overlap but no contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four words with a settled market meaning; nothing ambiguous is named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with exclusion (e) (c009) and exclusion (g) (c011) and is not contradicted elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Business to the extent that it is reinsured outside of this agreement' is genuinely vague — it does not say whether it means other reinsurance of the same layer, any other cession, or only duplicative cover, and 'to the extent' invites a proportional argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Offset article (c032) expressly contemplates 'any other reinsurance agreement heretofore or hereafter entered into between the REINSURED and the CORPORATION', showing other reinsurance exists, but nothing squarely contradicts this exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause carries an internal numerical mismatch ($9,000,000 each occurrence against a stated '$93,000,000 annual aggregate') and never says whether the 'annual aggregate' runs per ceded policy, per insured, or per agreement year.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This article is deleted and replaced twice — by Amendment No. 1 (c056, $25M limits) and Amendment No. 4 (c076, with a Nursing Home sub-limit and a deemed-occurrence rule) — each with its own date trigger, so three versions must be harmonised across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening words limit 'loss' to amounts 'within applicable policy limits', yet sub-paragraphs (b) and (c) capture 90% of amounts paid in excess of policy limits and punitive/exemplary damages, and (c) conditions recovery on the CORPORATION having 'counseled with' and 'concurred in' the REINSURED's course of conduct — all fertile ground for construction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with Article V (c017) on claim expenses, with the exclusion of claim expenses at the end, and with the Insolvency Clause (c046), whose insolvency measure of liability must be squared with the proviso here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'as will reduce the loss ultimately borne by the CORPORATION to what it would have been had the recovery preceded any payment' formula is mechanical and standard, and 'after expenses' is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Accounting Schedule (c021) credits to profits 'all salvage received by the CORPORATION', which is consistent with this recovery-sharing rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition anchors claim expenses to 'the supplementary payments provisions of the REINSURED'S policy' but then includes 'allocated investigation, adjustment, and legal expenses', which may not fall under those provisions — a general/specific mismatch about what the word 'including' adds.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article IV excludes claim expenses from 'loss' and Article V (c017) shares them pro rata, while the Accounting Schedule (c021) charges 'losses and claims expenses paid by the CORPORATION' to profits, so the definition's reach affects several other provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two narrow, concrete carve-outs (employee salaries; statutory unfair practice penalties); nothing to name as ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably with the loss definition (c013), which itself allows 90% recovery for punitive damages in defined circumstances, though the boundary between an excluded 'statutory penalty' and a covered punitive award is arguable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso refers to claim expenses 'connected with such settlement or appeal' although no settlement has been mentioned in the sentence, and the 'benefit derived by the CORPORATION' ratio is undefined in operation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short mechanical premium clause pointing to an attached Rating Schedule; nothing internally ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'Rating Schedule, attached hereto' was deleted and replaced by Schedule-A (c057) and then Schedule-B (c077), so the referent of this clause changes over time, but the substitutions are express.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single flat percentage; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Accounting Schedule (c021) credits premium 'net after ceding commission', which is consistent with this 25% figure, and no amendment alters it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The accounting-period machinery is internally inconsistent as written — a new period commences 'on January 1st of every other year' and runs twenty-four months, yet the final period is said to commence on the 'fifth January 1st preceding the termination date' — and the opening sentence is materially incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c052) deletes the first paragraph of this article and substitutes a 40% net-profit formula capped at the first $1,000,000 of limits, and c025 defers all further contingent commission after termination, so the article can only be applied by reconciling three texts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The credits and charges list is scrambled in numbering and the overhead charge keys to 'Item i of Credits to Profits' without a clearly identified item, leaving the computation ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with Amendment No. 1's cap of contingent commission to 'the first $1,000,000 of reinsured limits as respects each policy' (c052), since this schedule credits the whole written premium and charges all losses without any layer restriction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defining unpaid losses on 'the reserve of individual cases as developed to the date the computation is made' leaves the reserving judgment — and whose reserves control — unspecified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds directly into the Accounting Schedule charge for unpaid losses (c021) and the deficit definition (c023), which are consistent with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain arithmetic definition of deficit with a carry-forward rule; nothing to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the 'deficit, if any, at the end of the previous accounting period' charge in the Accounting Schedule (c021) and the net profit definition (c024).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line arithmetic definition; unambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c052) speaks of 'net profit accruing to the REINSURED', whereas the credits/charges here compute the CORPORATION's result, a small but real mismatch of referent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is garbled and, as written, both bars any accounting period commencing on or after termination and suspends all further contingent commission 'until all the reinsurance premium ... shall have been earned and all losses ... shall have been paid' — an open-ended deferral of uncertain duration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It stands in tension with the same article's promise of computations 'annually thereafter' and payment of 'the full contingent commission' when a computation shows a net profit (c020), and with Amendment No. 1's substituted formula (c052).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A bordereau on a form satisfactory to the CORPORATION' confers unilateral discretion and 'the amount due the CORPORATION' is not itself computed here, but the timing rules are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the premium article (c018) and the offset article (c032); nothing contradicts the 20-day reporting and remittance cycle.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Prompt notice ... of any event or development which might result in a claim upon the CORPORATION' uses two elastic terms — 'prompt' and 'might result' — which are the standard battleground in reinsurance late-notice disputes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Insolvency Clause (c047) restates the same duty to investigate, settle and defend and imposes a 'reasonable time' notice standard on a liquidator, and Article X (c031) gives inspection rights; these are compatible but set different notice yardsticks.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In the judgment of the CORPORATION' makes the trigger subjective, but the right conferred (join at its own expense) is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the REINSURED's exclusive control of claims in the first paragraph of Article IX (c027) and the reinsurer's defence rights in the Insolvency Clause (c047), without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Promptly' and 'satisfactory evidence of payment' are soft, but the obligation and its condition are otherwise plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside the advance-funding sentence (c030), which appears to relieve the REINSURED of paying first — the two payment mechanics must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is materially defective as written ('will furnish to the REINSURED the CORPORATION'S Payment of loss ... on the date on which the REINSURED proposes to make payment'), and 'advance notice' is not quantified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the reimbursement-on-proof rule in c029, so which governs a particular loss payment depends on harmonising the two paragraphs of Article IX.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single broad sentence with no time, place or notice limits — broad, but not ambiguous in a way a court must resolve.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere restricts or expands the inspection right; the reporting article (c026) is complementary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any balance ... under any other reinsurance agreement heretofore or hereafter entered into' is deliberately broad, and the closing words 'whether acting as assuming reinsurer or ceding company' leave the mutuality of the offset arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion (g) (c011) excludes business reinsured outside this agreement while this article reaches across other agreements, and the Insolvency Clause (c049) preserves the parties' status — points of friction, but no direct contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In no event exceeding 12 months plus odd time' uses an undefined trade phrase, and 'discovery period coverages or extended reporting endorsements attaching to ceded policies in force prior to or as of the effective date in time of cancellation' is syntactically broken.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Stipulation of Termination (c099) terminates the agreement only 'with respect to loss under policies issued on or after January 1, 1998', which does not obviously track this run-off machinery, and Article I (c001) limits the agreement to policies effective before the termination date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard market nuclear pool exclusion; the phrase 'formed for the purpose of covering atomic or nuclear energy risks' is concrete.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a physical-damage exclusion in a liability reinsurance treaty covering only liability lines (Article I, c001), so its practical fit is odd but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'except that this paragraph shall not operate where the REINSURED does not have knowledge' carve-outs are conditional and the text is fragmentary, leaving the exception's scope arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is boilerplate keyed to a 1960 approval regime and is not tied to any operative provision of this hospital treaty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Named hazard specifically insured against' is a defined-enough concept in market usage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A grandfathering rule with dates and an 'expiry date or [31 December]... whichever first occurs' formula; mechanically clear apart from transcription noise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Narrow and standard: loss accruing as member of or subscriber to a nuclear energy association.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three multipliers stated numerically; nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three stated multipliers; purely arithmetic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: They correspond to the territory definitions in c080 and c081 with no mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Incidental owned automobile exposure' is a vague threshold concept, though the two triggers that displace it (ambulances on emergency runs; more than 10 owned automobiles) are concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article I (c001, c070) and the Schedule of Underlying Limits (c002) cover Automobile Liability, and this rating rule is consistent with that grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The entry gives a bare number ('-125') without stating whether it is a multiplier, a credit or a percentage, and 'umbrella excluding BPL' appears to be a mistranscription of 'PL'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel entries in the Nursing Home and Facility sections of the same schedule (c092, c098) give different values, so the schedule does not resolve the figure internally.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The table gives the same 35% credit for both the second and third years, which departs from the descending pattern and from the earlier schedule and looks like a transcription or drafting error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Rating Schedule-A (c064) sets 45% for the second year and an 18% mature rate, so the substituted table conflicts with its predecessor, though by express substitution under c077.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Promising that 'an extended reporting endorsement will be issued at no additional cost' if the insured continues on an occurrence basis leaves the reinsurance consequences of that free tail unaddressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article I as amended (c070) recognises a 'claims-conversion basis' and Article I's discovery-period paragraph (c003) allows a separate limit of liability for such endorsements, so this free-tail promise interacts directly with the limit structure and the run-off rule in Article XI (c033).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two credits keyed to a bright-line bed count, with an express carve-out for minimum premiums.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the minimum premium tables that follow in the same schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The rate depends on 'OHIC's Manual GL and Professional Liability Premium (before application of experience and schedule rating)', a figure controlled by one party and not defined in the treaty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Facility Rating section (c093) uses the same construct with a different factor and refers to 'the REINSURED'S' manual premium, which is the same thing under Amendment No. 3 (c068).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allowing modification 'by schedule credit or debit at the REINSURED'S discretion but not to exceed 25% for a credit' caps credits but leaves debits uncapped and the discretion unstructured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Facility counterpart (c095) is drafted identically but names OHIC rather than the REINSURED; after Amendment No. 3 these are the same entity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of limits and the list of percentages are set out in separate blocks so that pairing them requires inference, and the total is described as 'the next $9,000,000' against ten enumerated millions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article III as amended (c076(b)) caps nursing home business at $10,000,000 each occurrence, which matches the ten-million rating structure here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Each million in limits is subject to a minimum premium of $1,000,000' states a minimum premium equal to the entire limit, which is commercially impossible and plainly a mechanical error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Every other minimum premium table in the schedules is expressed in thousands (c097 aside), so the figure cannot be reconciled with the rest of the rating structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The bare figures '25' and '258' are given without units and differ from the corresponding entries elsewhere in the same schedule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Hospital and Facility versions of the same line (c084, c098) give '-125' and '-is'/'25', so the schedule contradicts itself on the Indiana/Wisconsin factor and the contingent-endorsement charge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It carves out 'Imaging (MRI) risks' from the general method and keys the rest to the REINSURED's own manual premium, both workable but dependent on undefined classifications.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements the Nursing Home section (c088) and the outpatient facility coverage added by Amendment No. 4 (c070), though exclusion (j) (c074) removes laboratories and surgicenters from cover altogether.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A receipts-based rate table with stated figures; 'receipts' is undefined but the mechanic is otherwise concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers back to 'the First Million rates and the excess factors from the preceding paragraph' for owned automobiles, a cross-reference that resolves against c093.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Discretionary schedule credit or debit capped only on the credit side, exercisable at OHIC's discretion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors the Nursing Home credit provision (c089) and does not conflict with the minimum premium provisions it expressly excepts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean list of descending percentages applied to a defined 'modified First Million price'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the Facility rating base in c093 and c095 and with the ten-million structure used elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A minimum premium of '$1,500,000' for the first million of cover, and '$1,000,000' for each additional million, is on its face an impossible figure and reads as a misplaced decimal or dropped qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The hospital minimum premium tables in the same schedule run in thousands, so this entry cannot be reconciled with the rating structure as a whole; the Nursing Home version (c091) repeats the same error.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The values are given as bare, partly illegible figures ('-is', '25') with no units or explanation of application.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The two parallel entries in the same schedule (c084, c092) give different numbers for what appears to be the same factor, an inconsistency the instrument does not resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Termination is expressed 'with respect to loss under policies issued on or after January 1, 1998' — 'issued' is a different trigger from the 'becoming effective' language used throughout Article I, and the sentence does not say what happens to losses under earlier policies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article XI (c033) provides its own termination machinery — 90 days' notice, continuation of in-force policies for up to '12 months plus odd time', and continued cover for attaching discovery periods — none of which this stipulation addresses, so the run-off obligations after 1 January 1998 must be reconciled between the two.
